summary: Monier Monier-Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Oxford, King's College School, and the East India Company College under Horace Hayman Wilson. He taught at the East India Company College and Cheltenham before serving as Oxford's Boden Professor (1860-1887).

Monika Boehm-Tettelbach works in Indology and religious studies. She studied under Heinz-Jürgen Pinnow at Free University of Berlin and completed her Habilitation at Bonn. Her career includes professorships at the University of Bonn (1979), Cologne (1989-1990), and Heidelberg (1990-2006).
Monika Nowakowska is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. Her academic career includes affiliations with the University of Warsaw, where she is attested between 2010 and 2026.

Monika Zin works in Indology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Jagiellonian University, the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna, and the University of Munich. She held professorships at Munich (c. 2000-2015) and Freie Universität Berlin (c. 2014-2016).
Moodeen Sheriff was active in medicine and Indology. He studied at Madras Medical College and served as Native Surgeon at the Triplicane Dispensary from 1858 to 1889.

Moriichi Yamazaki works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University and the University of Cambridge under K. R. Norman. He later served as associate professor at Sendai National College of Technology and president of Hosen Gakuen College.

Moritz Abraham Stern was a scholar in mathematics and linguistics. He studied at Heidelberg and Göttingen under Carl Friedrich Gauss and Karl Otfried Müller, subsequently serving as a professor at the University of Göttingen from 1829 to 1884.

Moriya Okano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied at Kanto Gakuin University. He has held positions at Musashino University and as director of the Samgraha Institute for Psychological and Spiritual Studies.

Moriz Haupt was a scholar of linguistics and classical literature. He studied under Gottfried Hermann at the University of Leipzig, where he taught as professor from 1841 to 1851, before serving as professor at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1853.

Moriz Winternitz was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna under Georg Bühler and with Friedrich Max Müller. He taught at the German University Prague from 1902 to 1934 and at Visva-Bharati University.

Morten Schlütter is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen, Komazawa University, and Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. He has taught at Victoria University of Wellington and serves as associate professor at the University of Iowa.

Mortimer Wheeler was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London. He directed the National Museum of Wales and the London Museum, and served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1944 to 1948.

Morton Klass was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at Brooklyn College and Columbia University, where he was mentored by Conrad M. Arensberg. He held teaching posts at Bennington College, Barnard College, and Columbia University.
Mother Sayamagyi was a teacher in Buddhist studies and religious studies who studied as a disciple under Sayagyi U Ba Khin and eventually succeeded him.

Motohiro Yoritomi was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao and Yuichi Kajiyama. He held a professorship at Shuchiin University, where he taught from 1973, and later at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.

Motoi Ono is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tsukuba under Yasunori Ejima and earned a doctorate at the University of Vienna, later serving as associate professor at Tsukuba.

Mou Zongsan was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking University under Shili Xiong. He taught at various institutions, including National Taiwan Normal University, the University of Hong Kong, and the New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies.

Moumita Hossain is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She conducted doctoral research under the supervision of Ranjit Sen and has held an appointment as a research scholar and fellow at The Asiatic Society.

Mrinalkanti Gangopadhyaya is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held academic positions at Vidyasagar College in the 1970s and 1990, and served as a lecturer in the Sanskrit Department at the University of Calcutta.

Mudagamuwe Maithrimurthi works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and held posts at the University of Leipzig, Heidelberg University, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
